clue.text: Heavy rock star minced and moulded this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American singer famous for 'Bat Out of Hell'

definitions.note: a cryptic description: the dish is made of minced meat moulded into a loaf
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dish of minced meat pressed into a loaf shape and baked

explanation.surface: Someone took a big rock singer, put him through the mincer and shaped him into something.
explanation.walkthrough: The star's name and the dish are the same two words; 'this' points back at the star, so the clue reads as the singer being minced and moulded into his own namesake.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat Loaf was a stage name of a hard-rock singer, and meatloaf is also the baked dish of shaped minced beef.

clue.text: Handle Lewinksy's first broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so we want a word that sounds like the name rather than one spelt like it

parts.note: the first name of Monica Lewinsky, the White House intern in the Clinton scandal

explanation.surface: A tip on dealing with the airing of the first part of the Lewinsky story.
explanation.walkthrough: MONICKER is an accepted spelling of moniker. The clue's 'Lewinksy' is the setter's own misspelling of Lewinsky. 'Handle' looks like a verb but is the noun for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is informal slang for a person's name or nickname, which is exactly what a moniker is.

clue.text: (see 9ac.)
Pour forth and f— enjoy!

parts.note: the dashed-out swear word is written as the letter F, spelt out as a word
to enjoy something can mean to have the use or benefit of it

explanation.surface: A crude invitation to gush and then go and have a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff' is the polite stand-in for the four-letter word, as in 'effing and blinding'.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to flow or pour out, as a liquid or as words of praise do.

clue.text: Queer object, a butt

parts.note: an offensive slang word for a gay man
an object or aim is an end, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A crude playground insult: some odd thing is a figure of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' looks like a target of jokes, but it is the stub of a cigarette; in Britain a fag is a cigarette, so its stub is a fag end.
explanation.definitionFit: The burnt-out stub left of a smoked cigarette is called a butt, and in British slang a fag end.

clue.text: Shook the woman no end, like a cow

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off the word before it

parts.note: the pronoun for a woman
having an udder, as a cow does

explanation.surface: Someone rattled a woman ceaselessly, like a cow — a comic, unflattering scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shook the woman' reads as an action done to her, but 'Shook' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shudder is to tremble or shake violently, so shuddered is the past tense meaning shook.

clue.text: Some swear by one that's firm without looking inflamed

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
inflamed skin looks red

explanation.surface: A cream or remedy some people swear by for firm skin without redness.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening reads like an advert for a skin product, but 'Some swear by one' is the definition: a credo is a creed, something people swear by.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief, the kind of creed that its followers swear allegiance to.

clue.text: Pound Cameron's head to get on

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter

parts.note: David Cameron, then the new Conservative leader
to get on is to grow older

explanation.surface: A call to batter the Tory leader's head so as to make progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like a verb to hit, but it is the noun: an enclosure where stray animals are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an enclosure for confining animals, and a cage is likewise an enclosure that confines them.

clue.text: Latest exposure of member's an intrusion on the viewer

parts.note: the latest is the news
to flash is to expose one's private parts

explanation.surface: A man exposing himself is an unwelcome intrusion for anyone watching.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a flasher; the definition is a television bulletin that cuts into scheduled programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a brief bulletin that interrupts normal broadcasting, intruding on what the audience was watching.

clue.text: Titled bloke, going topless, gets "wood" in place of entertainment

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a knight is titled Sir
in golf a wood is a kind of club

explanation.surface: A nobleman stripping off and getting an erection at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' and 'wood' (slang for an erection) set up a seedy strip-club scene; the inverted commas mark 'wood' as used in another sense, the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue open late offering music, dancing and drinks, a place people go for entertainment.

clue.text: (& 10/3) Achieving your death? One method is shagging

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: bringing about your own end, i.e. dying
second meaning: British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A dark joke that sex is one way to die.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for having sex; read word by word, 'your end' is your death. The question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means succeeding in having sex, which is what shagging (British slang for intercourse) is.

clue.text: (see 9ac.)
Penis ring swallowed by one-time love bird

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside whatever swallowed it

parts.note: slang for the male organ
a means one
T is the abbreviation for time
a ring is round like the letter O
love is nil in tennis scores, written as O

explanation.surface: A cock ring swallowed by a former girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time love' reads as an ex, but it splits into three single letters, and the ring goes inside them. 'Bird', British slang for a girlfriend, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot of Australasia, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Rev. does fuss about party — let the dope get out of control

definitions.text: let the dope get out of control
definitions.note: a cryptic paraphrase of taking too much of a drug

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the jumbled letters surround the next word
a fuss is a commotion, stirring the preceding words into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, the abbreviation plus the verb
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A vicar fussing at a party where the drugs run riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev.' looks like the clergyman, but its letters join 'does' as anagram material, and 'dope' is a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdose is to take a dangerously excessive amount of a drug, letting one's drug use run beyond safe limits.

clue.text: Current outspoken Shah

indicators.note: outspoken here means spoken out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an eddy is a swirling current of water or air

explanation.surface: A forthright Shah of Iran who is fashionable right now.
explanation.walkthrough: Shah is not the Persian monarch but Eddie Shah, the British newspaper owner who took on the print unions in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Shah was a well-known British media entrepreneur, so his surname clues his first name.

clue.text: Mostly worried about nothing following business procedure to divert motions

indicators.note: following tells us the jumbled part comes after the business abbreviation

parts.note: CO, short for company, a business

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap around the next item
worried in the sense of disturbed or harried, so the word before it is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
zero, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone largely anxious over nothing after a business meeting about blocking parliamentary motions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like an instruction to drop a letter but is anagram material in full, and 'motions' are bowel movements, not proposals at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A colostomy is surgery that reroutes the bowel through an opening in the abdomen, diverting bowel movements.

clue.text: (see 26ac.)
Administer a handjob, say (and go through the experience again without energy)?

parts.note: the setter's reading: to give someone sexual relief is a euphemism for this act

parts.words: (and go through the experience again without energy)?
parts.note: a bonus aside: drop the letter for energy and the word becomes the verb meaning to live through again

explanation.surface: A sexual favour that one might replay later in memory, but without much vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside is not wordplay for the answer but a joke about it: remove E, the abbreviation for energy, and RELIEVE becomes RELIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to ease their tension, and giving 'relief' is a common euphemism for a sexual favour.

clue.text: Am screwing around with benzol — decorate my arms!

indicators.note: screwing around means twisting about, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; benzol is a crude form of benzene

explanation.surface: A sleazy chemist on solvents asking for a tattoo on his arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' are not limbs but a coat of arms, the heraldic shield.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to adorn a heraldic coat of arms with its devices, so it means decorating someone's arms.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) Definitive smack dose

parts.note: the definite article, the word that makes things definite
a clap is a sharp blow or slap

explanation.surface: The ultimate measured portion of heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' and 'dose' set up heroin, but smack is a slap and a dose is slang for venereal infection. The clap is slang for gonorrhoea.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, catching 'a dose' means contracting a venereal disease, and the clap is gonorrhoea.

clue.text: Notwithstanding empty Tories' ideas

parts.note: notwithstanding means despite this, or though

indicators.note: an empty word has had its insides removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the Conservatives, as written

explanation.surface: A jibe that despite everything the Conservative party is short on ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty Tories' ideas' reads as a political dig, but 'empty' strips the word to its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts are ideas or notions formed in the mind, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Ex-editor's wrinkly organ

parts.note: surface reading: an ageing man's wrinkled body part
setter's reading: the magazine for older readers founded by Richard Ingrams, former editor of Private Eye

explanation.walkthrough: An organ is also a publication, and 'wrinkly' is British slang for an old person. Ingrams, the Eye's former editor, launched The Oldie in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oldie is the magazine started by a former Private Eye editor, aimed at elderly readers, so it is his old person's publication.

clue.text: Party leader missing from podium due to senility

indicators.note: with its leader missing, the word that follows loses its first letter

parts.note: a do is a party
a raised platform for speakers or performers

explanation.surface: A party leader absent from the platform because they are going senile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' looks like a politician, but 'Party' is a separate piece and 'leader' belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of feeble-mindedness that can come with old age, which is what senility describes.

clue.text: Ineffectual type, but he's no plonker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: figuratively, a powerless person who gets nothing done
second meaning: plonker is British slang both for an idiot and for a penis, which a castrated man lacks

explanation.walkthrough: 'He's no plonker' seems to defend the man's intelligence, since a plonker is a fool in British slang, but the word also means penis.
explanation.definitionFit: A eunuch is a castrated man, and the word is used figuratively for someone weak and without real power.

clue.text: Perform oral sex, getting stiff at first, which is a big setback

indicators.note: at first places the stiff part at the front, before the oral-sex word

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body
slang verb, as in blow job

explanation.surface: A sex act on someone getting aroused, which proves to be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' suggests arousal, but here it is a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A body blow is literally a punch to the torso and figuratively a severe setback or disappointment.

clue.text: Prince seen after wild LSD party

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the drug's letters are rearranged
seen after tells us the royal letter is placed at the end

parts.note: the abbreviation for the drug, letters jumbled
P is the abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: A royal spotted leaving a drug-fuelled party, tabloid-style.
explanation.walkthrough: The SDLP is the Social Democratic and Labour Party of Northern Ireland. 'Party' looks like the setting of the scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The SDLP is a nationalist political party in Northern Ireland, so it is an example of a party.

clue.text: It's flipping Brown in charge — what a disaster!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
tan is a brown colour
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An exasperated groan at the prospect of Gordon Brown taking charge as Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, as in 'flipping heck', but it turns the first word around. Brown was Chancellor and Labour's leader-in-waiting in 2006.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic sank on her maiden voyage, and her name is shorthand for any catastrophe or doomed enterprise.

clue.text: (see 18ac.)
(& 15) Had droopy tits, enveloping Leo's head — distasteful, so heavily criticized

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping around, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: drooped, as breasts do with age

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter

parts.note: the star sign, or the name
food that has gone off is unpleasant to eat

explanation.surface: Someone's sagging chest was so off-putting it drew harsh criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: To slag someone off is British slang for running them down.
explanation.definitionFit: To slag off is to criticise harshly, so slagged off means heavily criticised.

clue.text: Brandished when spelling out "Adam Wing" with cold heart?

definitions.note: a description of a thing, standing for the noun

indicators.note: heart means the very middle, so the cold letter goes in the centre
out in the sense of disordered or wrong, so the quoted words are rearranged

parts.note: the quoted name, used purely for its letters
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone spelling out a person's name, waving something, with an icy heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling out' looks like reading letters aloud, but 'spelling' is casting spells and 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician or witch waves a magic wand while casting a spell, so it is the thing brandished then.

clue.text: How the missionary gets his oats over?

definitions.text: How the missionary gets his oats over?

parts.words: How the missionary gets his oats over?
parts.note: surface reading: a churchman abroad finishing his porridge or his harvest

parts.words: How the missionary gets his oats over?
parts.note: setter's reading: in the missionary sexual position the man lies above his partner while getting his oats, slang for sex

explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your oats' is British slang for having sex, and the missionary position is the face-to-face one with the man uppermost; 'over' hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the missionary position the man is above his partner, so the phrase describes his location during sex.
